facts.text: Trafford got its name when residents renamed the town after a prominent landowner, because another Alabama town already used Union City.
Set among rolling hills along the Locust Fork of the Black Warrior River, Trafford preserves an active rail line and elevated trestle bridge that draw rail enthusiasts.
The Locust Fork of the Black Warrior River winds through Trafford’s northwest, shaping the town’s natural landscape.
Trafford was incorporated as a town in 1948, marking its formal establishment within Jefferson County.
Residents celebrate seasonal events, youth activities, and gatherings around Town Hall, churches, parks, and ballfields, keeping the town’s spirit alive.
Trafford sits about 26 miles north of downtown Birmingham, offering a quiet escape from the city’s bustle.
